metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day average), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust quickly; re-estimate mean reversion target at 1–2 days lag from sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true volatility during sentiment-driven corrections (e.g., sudden drops after positive sentiment); add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 3–7 day horizon.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion to prior 10-day average, model often holds too high a forecast; reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
